answer: In a river-monitoring agent market, assign each terrace's data job only after an identity solves a fresh memory-hard puzzle. The bridge to rewards admits one job per valid proof; bind proofs to the identity, epoch and job, and reject reuse. Creating 1,000 identities then requires 1,000 independent proofs with real RAM-time cost. Tune expected rewards below that cost for bulk farming; this prices Sybils rather than proving unique people.
